series: JLPT N3 grammar series; denominator = 220 Bunpro N3 entries (n3-coverage-matrix, frozen)
levelPolicy: Bunpro precedence (docs/jlpt-levels.md). jlpt 3 where the decisive item is N3 grammar (connectives, なぜなら, である against です in a text); jlpt 4 for transfer items whose decisive form is N4 (passive/causative, てあげる/てもらう, ている/てある/ておいた). No N2 labels: every decisive item has N3 or N4 support.

primarySources.use: N3 すると: 'and then; thereupon' — what happened next or was found after an action. Meanings and accepted spellings taken over from result-topic-connectives.
N3 その結果: an outcome produced by what came before.
N3 そこで: a step taken in response to the situation.
N3 ところが: contrary to expectation.
N3 ところで: topic change.
N3 つまり: restatement; すなわち accepted as in result-topic-connectives.
N3 却って: outcome opposite to the intention.
N3 一方で: two sides both true.
N3 代わりに: instead of.
やはり／矢張り listed by Bunpro as JLPT N3 vocabulary: 'as expected; after all; likewise'. Seen through a search result snippet only (the grammar-point URL returned 404); not fetched.

independentReview.method: Three blind single-facet reviews, each by a fresh agent with a different requested model family, given only the frozen render, raw set JSON, article and ledger: A linguistic correctness, B consistency and quiz safety, C learner comprehensibility. Findings were consolidated by the coordinator, applied by the author, and sent back to the original reviewers for a per-finding disposition.

designNotes: No elimination by 'already used': in every passage, the sibling slot is printed with wording outside the item's candidate set (instruction list, option labels, additionalCorrectOptions and acceptedAnswers, substrings included). Sibling passages under one example key may differ slightly. elimcheck reports 0.

Arranged result: てあった is the base answer and the intransitive 〜ていた is an accepted additionalCorrectOption (it reports the state without asserting how it arose). The base distractor is the preparer's action 〜ておいた, which is categorically wrong with a が-marked subject and a narrator who did not prepare it. The two arranged contexts use different scenes and cues (classroom-windows: the teacher's note on the board; late-inn: staff waiting up after a phone call).
Spontaneous states (window-wind, kitchen-light): the wind or forgetting contradicts a deliberate てあった, so 〜ていた is the only fit.

Prepared action (guest-room, cold-drinks): the narrator is the doer and the object is marked with を, so the intransitive 〜ていた is grammatically excluded and 〜ておいた is the key. guest-room prints the distractor in kana (あいていた) because 開いていた could be read ひらいていた, which is transitive (窓をひらく).

bakery-afternoon-b: the blank introduces the writer's own decision (〜てみようと思います). Its candidates are only すると／そこで (round 3): その結果 was removed because a present intention can itself be a result of the trial. すると presents the next development or discovery after an event and does not introduce the writer's own plan; そこで (a deliberate step chosen in response) is the key.

bakery-afternoon-a and street-lights-a: その結果 is the key; すると／そうすると is also accepted, because it simply presents what came after the event (additionalCorrectOptions, as in result-topic-connectives kekka-factory-output). The instruction names all three candidates for typed mode.
weekend-survey reframed so it no longer shares the library-rules frame: the alternative is 〜か、あるいは〜か (no のどちらか), the addition has no も, and the restatement is a closing summary without ということだ／ことになる.
Example keys changed in round 2: window-air -> classroom-windows, entrance-light -> late-inn; new keys guest-room and cold-drinks (prepared-action facet).
